exact_statement: For actual two-weight thresholds with independent interior product biases, let K_star be the complete max of the canonical squared-tail references, and r(U,T) the smaller nonzero jump count of the two directional physical coefficient profiles on an occupied mixed label. Then P(U,T)<=r(U,T)K_star(U,T), and C_star<=E_mixed+sum_mixed P ln r. The positive complete normalization tax is <=D_mixed ln2. For the gate with at most one zero among a+b inputs, a,b>=2, both profiles have at most two jumps at every bias, P<=2K_star, and for a=b=m the complete top-label ratio is 2-1/(m^2+(m-1)^2), proving factor2 sharp. It has a real two-weight representation for every1<w<2 and C_star<=(460+81ln2)Delta by the established symmetric-threshold baseline. Free pointwise P<=K_star and overlap sum min(K_A,K_B)>=M are false, already on a fair four-bit threshold. No unrestricted jump-count or universal signed-payment bound is asserted.
